Whether the Shang “Di” was a single supreme god is still disputed; the Shang practiced human sacrifice; and Confucian scholars point out that Shangdi governs all things without being the creator. Reading ancient texts as monotheism may be a projection by later readers.

blocks.h: A little-known prehistory

Looking for the Bible in ancient books was already done three hundred years ago. The French Jesuit Joachim Bouvet (1656–1730) developed “Figurism” at the Kangxi court, holding that the Book of Changes was the lost book of Enoch, hiding messianic revelation given to Adam. Today’s researchers see it as an extension of accommodation strategy and also note that it borrowed from European allegorical interpretation and mystical traditions. Similar contemporary works can be viewed in this context.
Let’s separate what is certain, what is disputed, and what is an inference of faith.

The Book of Songs odes “Dang,” “Daming” and “Huangyi” and the “Oath of Tang” in the Book of Documents do contain the “Shangdi” lines above. But scholars dispute when the individual chapters of the Book of Documents were composed, so they should not be taken as the words of Tang himself.

Shangdi and Di appear in Shang oracle-bone inscriptions, governing weather, harvests and war, and merged with “Heaven” in the Zhou. Whether Di was a single supreme god is still disputed (Eno raised the challenge).

The character 船 (“boat”) is a phono-semantic compound. The Shuowen gives it as “a boat; from 舟, with 鉛 abbreviated as the phonetic” (舟也。从舟，鉛省聲), and Duan Yucai revised this to “from 舟, with 㕣 as the phonetic” (从舟㕣聲). Both views take 舟 as the meaning component and the other part as the sound component. The breakdown “舟 + 八 + 口 = Noah’s family of eight” has no basis in the etymology.

Claims such as those in The Discovery of Genesis (by Kang and Nelson) and God’s Promise to the Chinese assume that Chinese characters secretly encode Genesis. Reviewers point out that the evidence is thin, that many of the breakdowns are actually phonetic components, and that some examples are even modern simplified characters. The Christian reviewer Doyle affirms the care behind Chan Kei Thong’s book, but has reservations about several of its identification claims and says it overlooks Shang human sacrifice.

The Catholic Church banned the Chinese rites in 1715, and in 1939, under Pope Pius XII, Plane Compertum permitted the faithful to take part in honoring Confucius and ancestors. The Protestant dispute over Shangdi and Shen ended with both editions in parallel.
The ancients’ reverence for Shangdi can be seen as a witness God left among all peoples. This is an interpretation of faith, which history can neither prove nor disprove.
He has not left any people alone

At Lystra Paul told a crowd of villagers who had never read the Scriptures that God had always been leaving evidence: the rains, the fruitful seasons, the food. In Athens he walked past an altar “to an unknown god” and neither smashed it nor worshiped at it. He simply said, the One you have been feeling after, I have come to tell you about.

He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons and the boundaries of their dwellings, that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.

So the farmer by the Yellow River who looked up and cried “Heaven” was not outside God’s sight. The poet of “Dang” sighs, “All have a beginning, but few see it through to the end.” People start well and rarely finish well. That sigh sits very close to the Bible’s diagnosis of humanity.

The ancient books also leave an unsolved question. Shangdi is high above, sacrifice to Heaven was the emperor’s business, and ordinary people could not even get near the door of that altar. How can anyone draw near to this One?
No one has seen God at any time. The only born Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared him.

The answer came from outside the Altar of Heaven: this God came down. He was born in a manger, died on a cross and rose on the third day. Fishermen, tax collectors and widows can call Him “Abba, Father.” So the gospel fulfills the ancients’ reverence, and it also renews what was wrong in China, the human sacrifice, the royal monopoly, the family idols. Both are true.

God, having in the past spoken to the fathers through the prophets at many times and in various ways, has at the end of these days spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom also he made the worlds.
Go outside tonight, stand for a minute and look up at the sky. Think of the poet three thousand years ago who looked up at the same sky.
Reflect: When I say “Heavens above” in daily life, to whom am I speaking in my heart? If that One knows my name, what would I like to say to Him?

Pray: Father in heaven, You have never forgotten this people. Thank You that when my ancestors were feeling their way, You were already not far from them. Lord Jesus, You came down and showed that distant Ruler to be my Father. Help me honor my ancestors and worship You alone. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Bible is my standard: We do not spread the gospel by breaking up characters. A good witness stands up to checking; what cannot be verified I put down, even if it sounds moving.

Change your mindset: Move from “Christianity is a foreign religion” to “God left evidence in this land long ago,” and from “the Bible was already in the ancient books” to “Christ brought something new that the ancients did not have.”

People matter more than tasks: Your elders worry that if you believe in Jesus you will abandon your ancestors. On the question of ancestor rites, honor the person first and discuss ritual afterward; the relationship matters more than winning the argument.

blocks.h: This week: Find an elder and ask them to tell you about the family’s ancestors: where they came from and what hardships they endured. Listen carefully and write it down. Let them know that, as a follower of Jesus, you value these things more than before.
Pass it on: As a child, did you ever hear adults cry out “Heaven above”? Who do you think the ancients were speaking to when they looked up and called to Heaven?
Quiz

quiz.q: Where does “Vast is Shangdi, ruler of the people below” come from?
o: The Book of Documents, “Oath of Tang”
The Book of Songs, Greater Odes, “Dang”
The Analects, “Bayi”
quiz.e: It comes from the Greater Odes, “Dang.” “I fear Shangdi, and dare not fail to set it right” is from the “Oath of Tang.”

quiz.q: How should we regard “船 = 舟 + 八 + 口, hinting at Noah’s family of eight”?
o: Dictionaries treat 船 as a phono-semantic compound, and this breakdown has no basis in the etymology
It has been confirmed by oracle-bone scholars
It is the original explanation in the Shuowen
quiz.e: The Shuowen gives “from 舟, with 鉛 abbreviated as the phonetic,” and Duan Yucai’s commentary gives “from 舟, with 㕣 as the phonetic.” A pleasing explanation is not the same as a well-founded one.

quiz.q: How was the dispute over the Chinese Bible’s term for God eventually handled?
o: Everyone standardized on “Shangdi”
The pope ruled for “Shen”
The Union Version is printed in both a “Shen” edition and a “Shangdi” edition
quiz.e: Both sides gave some ground. Both editions are still in print today.

units.title: Mackay and Missions in Taiwan
units.sub: A pair of dental forceps, a graft of skin that did not take, and a history that needs no prettifying.

share.v: And how will they preach unless they are sent? As it is written, “How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the Good News of peace, who bring glad tidings of good things!”

blocks.h: On March 9, 1872, a ship sailed into the mouth of the Tamsui River. A 27-year-old Canadian on board gazed at the hills on both banks, and later wrote in his memoirs of the voice he heard in his heart: “This is the place.” For the next 29 years he gave himself to this island.
What the islanders remember him by is a pair of dental forceps. By 1895 he had personally pulled more than 21,000 teeth, and his students and local co-workers had pulled about as many again.
He will not fail nor be discouraged, until he has set justice on the earth, and the islands wait for his law.
Mackay was not the first to come

The beginning of modern Christianity in Taiwan was in the south. The Scottish doctor James L. Maxwell began preaching and practicing medicine in Tainan on June 16, 1865, a day later kept as the founding anniversary of the Presbyterian Church in Taiwan. Only 23 days later, a rumor said he made medicine from human organs, his clinic was smashed, and he had to withdraw to Takao.
Seven years later Mackay arrived in the north and set up the three supports of his work:

items: Healing: quinine for malaria, tooth extraction, a hymn and then a sermon; in 1880 he built the Mackay Clinic (偕醫館) in Tamsui, the first Western-style medical institution in northern Taiwan.
Learning: the Oxford College (理學堂大書院) was completed in 1882, funded by $6,125 raised in his home county of Oxford County; in 1884 the Tamsui Girls’ School opened.

People: his first convert, Gan Chheng-hoa (嚴清華), later became the first local pastor in the north; in 1878 he married the Pingpu woman Tan Chhong-bing (張聰明), who served as dormitory matron at the girls’ school.

blocks.h: It is like opening a clinic in an unfamiliar village: the neighbors do not care about your theories, only whether you can help them sleep tonight. Once the tooth stops hurting, a person is willing to sit down and listen. Mackay’s own way of putting it was that the Bible and the forceps went together.
Dr. Landsborough’s skin

In 1928 Dr. David Landsborough of Changhua met a boy named Chiu Kim-iaw (周金耀), with festering wounds and a raging fever, close to death. Mrs. Landsborough (連瑪玉) offered to give skin from her own leg, and Landsborough cut four pieces and grafted them onto the boy’s leg. The graft in the end failed, but the boy’s life was saved. Chiu was adopted by the Landsboroughs and later became a pastor and moderator of the Presbyterian Church in Taiwan.
The part that should not be glossed over

The missionaries came in after the treaty ports were opened. In 1868 a camphor dispute involving British merchants brought British warships; marines took Anping and a Qing official took his own life. The treaty that followed, besides camphor, also provided compensation for churches and forbade violence against missionaries and believers. In local eyes, the cross and the gunboat were hard to tell apart.

During the Sino-French War of 1884–1885, many chapels in the north were destroyed and believers suffered; when Mackay returned, he demanded 10,000 Mexican silver dollars in compensation. He was also hard to get along with: he fell out with each of his first three co-workers, and the mission even questioned his mental state. His marriage also drew comment, in Canada and among the foreign community on the island, at the time.
Let’s separate legend from historical fact.
Mackay arrived at Tamsui on March 9, 1872, and died of throat cancer at Tamsui on June 2, 1901.
At Mackay’s death the northern church had about 60 chapels, 60 preachers, and nearly 1,800 communicants.

The tooth-pulling numbers come from him: his memoirs say he personally pulled more than 21,000, and elsewhere he says that over 30 years the total was 40,000. If the latter includes those pulled by his students, the two roughly fit, but neither has been confirmed by a third-party count.

“Better to burn out than to rust out” is often called Mackay’s motto (some translations say “decay” or “corrode”). We have not yet found a source in his own hand; similar words also appear in biographies of George Whitefield, so he seems not to have coined it. It is safer to treat it as a later summary of his life.

These people’s service shows the power of the gospel, while their flaws and their complicity with their times remind us that the glory belongs to God. This is an interpretation of faith, a conclusion history itself does not draw.
Perspectives Room
How should we assess this missionary history? Here are several serious views side by side.

items.h: The missionary enterprise profited from treaties and gunboats, treated Western civilization as the only standard, and did cultural harm. The treaty of 1868 is a clear example, and this tension cannot be skipped.

The protagonists of the history include Taiwanese people: Gan Chheng-hoa, Tan Chhong-bing, local preachers and believers. The faith quickly had local leaders and sufferers, who were not passive recipients.
Many missionaries gave themselves up sincerely, leaving hospitals and schools and burying themselves here. Purity of motive and structural problems can both be true.

blocks.h: The Lord who bore it Himself

Mrs. Landsborough’s skin did not grow on the boy’s leg in the end. Years later Chiu Kim-iaw told the Landsboroughs’ son that although your mother’s flesh did not grow on my leg, it is forever attached to my heart. Human self-giving often has limits like this: surgery fails, people have tempers, an age binds them.
These stories point to a deeper physician. He did not send someone else but came among us Himself, healing us with His own wounds, and this self-giving was not in vain.
He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live to righteousness. You were healed by his wounds.
In his 1888 report Mackay handed the credit back: the glory is to be given to God, who blessed small efforts. God uses clay jars, and clay jars have cracks, which is exactly the point.
But we have this treasure in clay vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God and not from ourselves.
Find a map of Taiwan and look for a hundred-year-old church or hospital near where you live. Think: who walked here in the beginning? Who was the first to open a door and welcome them?
Reflect: Which grace that I enjoy reached my hands because others sweated and wept for it?

Pray: Lord who sends servants, thank You for remembering the islands. Thank You for those who came here, and forgive the church for the times it walked beside power. Lord Jesus, You bore my wounds Yourself; make me a blessing to those around me. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Jesus is my example: He went through all the cities and villages and saw people’s suffering first. Service starts with the other person’s need tonight.
Let Jesus receive all the glory: Even Mackay had a temper and flaws. Do not idolize spiritual predecessors, and do not idolize yourself.
Life first, then relationships, then ministry: Mackay’s most lasting fruit was people like Gan Chheng-hoa. Nurturing one person often goes further than finishing one task.

blocks.h: This week: Look up the first person to preach the gospel in your area or its earliest church, and tell the story to a family member; then think of one small pain you can solve for a neighbor and do it this week.

Pass it on: Did you know that many of Taiwan’s earliest Western-style hospitals and schools were founded by foreign missionaries together with local believers? What do you think makes people willing to stay in a foreign land for a lifetime?
Quiz

quiz.q: Why was the clinic James Maxwell opened in Tainan soon smashed?
o: He refused to see patients
A rumor said he made medicine from human organs
The Qing court ordered it closed
quiz.e: On July 9, 1865, the rumor triggered violence and he withdrew to Takao.

quiz.q: What was the result of the skin graft the Landsboroughs performed for Chiu Kim-iaw?
o: The graft was a complete success
The boy unfortunately died
The graft failed, but the boy lived and became a pastor
quiz.e: The surgery did not succeed, but the love stayed in his heart and in history.

quiz.q: How should “Better to burn out than to rust out” be regarded?
o: It is often credited as Mackay’s motto, but this unit has not found a source in his own hand
It has been confirmed as carved on his tombstone
It was the first sentence of his memoirs
quiz.e: It can inspire us, but there is no need to state a source that has not been verified.

units.title: Hudson Taylor and the Chinese Church
units.sub: A queue, four graves, a treaty that put the Bible and opium on one sheet of paper, and the Chinese who took up the baton.

share.v: Most certainly I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.

blocks.h: In August 1867 he buried his eight-year-old daughter. In February 1870 his son died on a boat on the Yangtze. On July 20 of the same year, a baby only 13 days old died; three days later his wife Maria was gone too, at 33. Three years, four graves, all in China.
His name was Hudson Taylor. After that he stayed on in this land for another thirty-five years. Why would a person not leave? That question deserves a seat and some thought.
Most certainly I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
It began with a queue

Hudson Taylor arrived in Shanghai on March 1, 1854, at the age of 21. He soon did something the foreign community could hardly bear: he shaved his head, grew a queue and wore Chinese clothes. Foreigners in Shanghai mocked his team as the “pigtail gang.” On June 25, 1865, on the beach at Brighton, England, he resolved to found the China Inland Mission, for the inland provinces beyond the treaty ports where there were no missionaries. In May 1866 he set out with 16 new co-workers aboard the Lammermuir.

It is like visiting someone’s home: you take off your leather shoes and put on their slippers, and the host feels at ease. But if you arrived in your big brother’s tank, however quickly you changed into slippers, people would still look out the window first. Taylor could change his clothes, but the tank was not something he could change.
Bible and opium on the same sheet of paper

The Treaty of Tianjin of 1858 on one hand declared that Christianity was not to be treated as a harmful superstition and permitted missionary work, and on the other effectively legalized the import of opium. Both things were written into the same set of treaties, signed by a defeated Qing. The missionaries’ right to enter the interior also came from this set of treaties.

Earlier, when Morrison arrived in China in 1807, the East India Company would not carry missionaries, so he went by way of New York and reached Macau on an American ship; in 1809, to be able to stay legally, he took a post as the Company’s translator, which he held until his death. In 27 years he baptized only about ten people.

Taylor himself opposed the opium trade: in 1888 he moved at the London missionary conference for its “complete suppression,” and before 1894 he also testified before the British Royal Commission on Opium. His position was clear, and who opened the road he walked on is just as clear.
Yangzhou and 1900

In 1868 a mob in Yangzhou attacked the China Inland Mission’s residence, setting fire to it and looting, and the British consul sent gunboats to apply pressure. Opinion in London condemned Taylor for nearly causing a war, and in 1869 the House of Lords even debated the value of missions. In the Boxer events of 1900, the Mission lost 58 adults and 21 children, and of 88 workers in Shanxi, 47 were killed. In total, at least 189 Protestant missionaries and their children died. Chinese believers died in far greater numbers, but the estimates vary widely and there is no reliable total. Taylor refused to accept compensation for lost property and lives.
Chinese hands took the baton

items: Liang Fa: a believer from Morrison’s time, the first Protestant in China to be ordained as an evangelist.

John Sung (1901–1944): a PhD in chemistry from Ohio State University who returned to China to become an itinerant revivalist, traveling among Chinese communities in Southeast Asia and reaching Singapore in 1935.

Wang Mingdao (1900–1991): refused for theological reasons to join the Three-Self movement and was arrested in August 1955; after retracting a confession he had been pressed to sign in 1958, he was imprisoned again and was not released until 1979 or 1980.

Watchman Nee (1903–1972): arrested in 1952 and sentenced to 15 years in 1956; he was not released when his term ended and died in prison in 1972. His writings still circulate in Chinese churches worldwide today, though the Assembly Hall tradition he founded is also controversial.

blocks.h: The lives above can be found in the Biographical Dictionary of Chinese Christianity and in the Asia Harvest accounts.
The two paths of the church in China today

A timeline of facts: the Three-Self Manifesto was issued in 1950; the Three-Self Patriotic Movement was formally established in 1954; around 1952 all foreign missionaries left; during the Cultural Revolution of 1966–1976 all churches were closed and worship went underground; in 1979–1980 the Three-Self churches were restored and the China Christian Council was founded; unregistered house churches have existed alongside, and in recent years have come under tighter control; in 2018 the religious affairs administration was merged into the United Front Work Department.

items.h: Missions were bound up with the unequal treaties, and although Taylor opposed opium, his work still benefited from the treaties. The Mission’s approach nearly brought force down in the Yangzhou incident, and its practice of not reporting to consuls also displeased British officials.

He gave up the comfort of his homeland, went to the interior where no one went, refused compensation, and paid the highest price in his own family. By 1905 the Mission had 825 members, more than 300 stations and about 25,000 believers.

Changing clothes was only the first step. The 500-plus Chinese workers of the time were called “helpers,” and leadership remained in foreign hands. A truly Chinese church would show its independent face only with the generation of Wang Mingdao and Watchman Nee.

items.n: How to view the church in China today
items.h: Some think one should serve within the registered churches, and others think conscience cannot allow registration. Both sides have real believers and real costs. This unit states facts only and passes no political judgment.

blocks.h: Biographies are the easiest place for things to go astray. Let’s check.
Hudson Taylor arrived in Shanghai on March 1, 1854, founded the China Inland Mission in 1865, and died in Changsha on June 3, 1905. His wife Maria and three of his children died in China.
The 1858 Treaty of Tianjin contained both provisions permitting missionary work and provisions that effectively legalized the import of opium.
In 1900 the China Inland Mission lost 58 adults and 21 children, the heaviest losses of any mission that year.

How many Christians are there in China? No one knows for certain. An official 2018 white paper gives 38 million Protestants; the China General Social Survey shows about 2% of adults identifying as Christian (2010–2018); the Center for the Study of Global Christianity estimates about 7% of the population in 2020, and Asia Harvest about 9%. Pew believes growth appears to have leveled off, while admitting that surveys may undercount. Round figures such as “100 million believers” should be cited with caution.
In Singapore’s 2020 census, 18.9% of all residents were Christian, and about 21.6% of Chinese residents.

New Zealand: in 1871 the Chinese evangelist Paul Ah Chin was commissioned; from 1879 Alexander Don preached to Chinese gold miners in Otago, baptizing about 20 people in 34 years, and the register of Chinese he compiled remains an important source for early Chinese history in New Zealand.
This history shows God using people who were limited, even bound by their times. This is an interpretation of faith, and it does not cancel the harm done by gunboat diplomacy.
He fell into the ground first
Taylor was willing to take off his suit because Someone had changed clothes before him.
who, existing in the form of God, didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men.

And their graves could bear fruit only because a grave came first. When Jesus spoke of the grain of wheat falling to the ground, He was speaking first of Himself. He was crucified, died, and on the third day rose from the dead; His death was never in vain, and that is why His followers dare to lay down their lives.

Cheap words have no place here. Taylor’s grief at losing his children was not one bit smaller for his faith, and the blood of those believers in Shanxi should not be lightly used as the arithmetic of revival. All we can say is this: God did not leave those standing beside the graves. He Himself has been in a grave.
I planted. Apollos watered. But God gave the increase. So then neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase.
Alexander Don baptized about 20 people in 34 years in New Zealand, and Morrison about 10 in 27 years, and by the measure of results neither passes. But growth is not their KPI. It is God’s.
Open the contacts on your phone and find the person who led you to Christ, then think about who led that person to Christ. Work backward as far as you can, until you can go no further.
Reflect: How many links in this chain that reached my hands were joined with tears, even with lives? And my link, to whom is it joined now?

Pray: Lord Jesus, You are the grain of wheat that fell into the ground. Thank You, and thank You for those who carried the gospel to the Chinese. Forgive them and us for walking beside power. Remember the brothers and sisters who are still suffering for You, and make me willing to fall as one grain. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Jesus is my example: He emptied Himself to come among us. What do the people you want to reach wear, say and fear? This week try putting on their slippers.
Selflessness overcomes the old self: It is no longer I, but Christ who lives in me. The grain falling to the ground means handing over my self-centered plans.
235 spiritual companions: Morrison had Liang Fa. Whom are you nurturing? Write down one name.

blocks.h: This week: Find out who started your church, or the Chinese church in your city, and tell the story to a teenager or a new friend; also pray once for a Chinese church that still faces hardship today.
Pass it on: How do you view the foreigners who came to China more than a hundred years ago and laid down their lives here? Do you think their connection to opium and gunboats can be separated?
Quiz

quiz.q: What was Hudson Taylor’s position on the opium trade?
o: He supported it because it brought the right to evangelize
In 1888 he moved for its complete suppression
He never took a stand
quiz.e: He opposed opium, but his right to enter the interior still came from the same set of unequal treaties. Both things must be said.

quiz.q: What is the more honest way to state the number of Christians in China today?
o: It is definitely 100 million
Official and academic figures differ widely, and no one knows for certain
It is definitely only 2%
quiz.e: The Pew synthesis says growth appears to have leveled off, and also cautions that surveys may undercount.

quiz.q: Alexander Don preached to Chinese laborers in New Zealand for 34 years. About how many did he baptize?
o: About 2,000
About 200
About 20
quiz.e: The number is small, but the register he left and his faithfulness endure. Fruitfulness cannot be counted only by results.

units.title: Facing the Church’s Dark History Honestly
units.sub: A friend asks, “Haven’t you Christians killed people too?” The answer is yes. This lesson defends no one; it opens the ledger and reads it line by line.

share.v: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

blocks.h: In the spring of 1096, a column marching under the banner of the cross moved along the Rhine. They were going to rescue the Holy Land, yet first, at their own doorstep, they killed at least 800 Jews in Worms and at least 1,100 in Mainz. In places, bishops opened their doors to shelter the Jews, but the column broke into the bishops’ residences and kept killing.
These people had been baptized and had sung hymns, and they felt they were serving God. Jesus had said long ago that people like this would come.
They will put you out of the synagogues. Yes, the time is coming that whoever kills you will think that he offers service to God.
The ledger is opened

items: The Crusades: the Rhineland massacres of 1096, the slaughter after the capture of Jerusalem in 1099, and the sack of Constantinople, a fellow Christian city, in 1204.

The Inquisition: the Spanish Inquisition lasted more than three hundred years, using torture to extract confessions and public executions, and its deepest harm fell on forced converts from Judaism and the descendants of Muslims.
Witch hunts: roughly 30,000 to 60,000 people were executed in Europe, most of them women, in both Catholic and Protestant regions.
Antisemitism: Luther wrote vicious anti-Jewish writings in 1543; in 1994 the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America formally repudiated them.
Slavery and colonialism: a papal bull of 1455 permitted the Portuguese king to conquer non-Christians; many Christians in the American South used the Bible to defend slavery.
Residential schools and sexual abuse: more than 150,000 Indigenous children in Canada were forced into government-funded Christian schools; for recent child sexual abuse and its cover-up, see Unit 6.

blocks.h: The details and numbers of these events are marked with their degree of certainty, item by item, in the next step.

A dentist is found to have prescribed the wrong medicine for years. We may argue over how many people he harmed, and we should find out; but whatever the number, it can never serve as evidence that he is innocent. Corrections to historical numbers work the same way.
Checking the numbers is not a way to get off the hook

Quite a few of the familiar numbers are exaggerated, and correcting them is the historian’s duty. On the Spanish Inquisition: in the nineteenth century Llorente claimed more than 30,000 executions, and modern archival research gives far lower figures; Contreras and Henningsen counted about 44,000 trials from 1540 to 1700 with 826 actual executions; Kamen estimates no more than 3,000 over the whole period, and some scholars estimate close to or slightly under 10,000. The claim of “nine million witches” in the witch hunts has been refuted.

Nor were the witch hunts all the work of church courts. Most executions came from secular courts and local authorities; the Inquisitions of Spain, Portugal and Italy in fact restrained large-scale witch hunts, and in the 1610s the Spanish inquisitor Salazar ended the Basque witch hunt. This does not clear the church: the secular judges were Christians too, and the demonology they believed was inseparable from what was preached.

The scale of the Jerusalem massacre is also debated. Kedar studied the accounts of Western historians, and Hirschler points out that early Arabic sources show that killing did occur, but that the narrative of a total massacre of the city took shape later. The slaughter did happen; its scale awaits further study.
At the very same time

During the Rhineland massacres, the bishops of Speyer, Mainz and other places stepped in to protect the Jews; in 1146 Bernard condemned attacks on Jews. In 1550, at Valladolid, Las Casas debated Sepúlveda and refuted the claim that the Indians were slaves by nature. These people cannot cancel the evil, but they show that when Christians condemned these atrocities, they used Jesus’ own words.
Let’s look at each claim separately and mark how certain it is.
In 1096 the Crusaders attacked the Jewish communities on the Rhine, killing at least 800 in Worms and at least 1,100 in Mainz; some bishops tried to protect them, mostly without success.

European witch hunts executed roughly 30,000 to 60,000 people; the “nine million” claim has been refuted; most were sentenced by secular courts, and most victims were women (proportions varied by place).

Modern estimates of Spanish Inquisition executions are mostly in the thousands, at most under about 10,000; methods differ among scholars, and the archives have gaps. Lower numbers do not mean that torture, expulsion and terror did not exist.

The church has made formal confessions: the Vatican’s Day of Pardon on March 12, 2000; the Southern Baptist Convention’s apology for slavery and racism in 1995; the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America’s repudiation of Luther’s anti-Jewish writings in 1994; the pope’s apology in Canada for the residential schools in 2022; and the Vatican’s repudiation of the “Doctrine of Discovery” in 2023.

These sins contradict Jesus’ teaching, so they cannot prove Jesus wrong. This is a theological judgment. A critic can reply that a religion’s fruit counts on its ledger too, and that reply deserves to be taken seriously.
Perspectives Room
What does the church’s dark history show?

items.h: If Christianity really has the power to change lives, why did Christian societies in power do evil for so long? If every good thing is credited to the faith and every bad thing blamed on “false believers,” the claim can never be refuted. That challenge is fair.

The Bible itself predicts that some will name the Lord’s name and do evil, and teaches that people are sinners. We are willing to admit that many wrongdoers were real church members and leaders, and their sins are our family shame. Good fruit cannot cancel bad fruit; what we can point to is the Lord who never sinned and His standard of judgment.

blocks.h: Jesus’ own verdict
The church’s sternest judge is not the atheist but Jesus. He said long ago that on that day some would come with impressive ministry reports and He would not recognize them.

“Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven, but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven. Many will tell me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, didn’t we prophesy in your name, in your name cast out demons, and in your name do many mighty works?’ Then I will tell them, ‘I never knew you. Depart from me, you who work iniquity.’
Daniel was a godly man, yet when he prayed he did not say “they”; he said “we.” He had not personally committed his ancestors’ sins, but he stood inside them and confessed.

Oh, Lord, the great and dreadful God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness with those who love him and keep his commandments, we have sinned, and have dealt perversely, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even turning aside from your precepts and from your ordinances.

The cross is the final verdict. The sinless Lord was nailed up by religious leaders, political power and a crowd that had sung hymns days before. He did not collect charges against them; He prayed for them. The church has a way back today only because of this grace.
Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.”
But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

On a piece of paper, write down a church-related harm you have heard of, or a wound you yourself have suffered, or something for which you have hurt someone else. You do not need to show it to anyone; just lay it before God.
Reflect: When I hear of a church scandal, is my first reaction to defend, to distance myself, or to grieve?

Pray: Righteous Lord, we have sinned, and our ancestors and the church have sinned too. Have mercy on those harmed in the name of the cross; You remember all their tears. Do not let us make excuses for ourselves. Thank You, Lord Jesus, for dying on the cross for sinners and rising to give us new life; make us bear fruit that fits repentance. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Humility overcomes pride: We do not have to be lawyers for two thousand years of church history. We can say, “Yes, that’s true, and I’m grieved.”

Let Jesus reign: Christians in power are the most dangerous. The Crusades and the Inquisition both claimed to act for the Lord, yet Jesus said His kingdom is not of this world; the church must leave its lust for power.
Selflessness: Repentance must bear fruit. Like Zacchaeus, make restitution after confessing, and accept that others may not forgive immediately.

blocks.h: This week: If you know someone who was hurt by the church or by Christians, ask, “Would you be willing to tell me what happened?” Then just listen, without defending. If someone is being harmed right now, help them find safety and professional help.
Pass it on: What is the thing the church has done that disappointed you most? I would like to hear your thoughts.
Quiz

quiz.q: Which statement about the witch-hunt numbers is closer to what modern historians say?
o: About nine million people were burned
About 30,000 to 60,000 people were executed, mostly by secular courts
No one was executed at all
quiz.e: The “nine million” claim has been refuted. Lower numbers do not mean innocence, and secular judges were Christians too.

quiz.q: Why check the number of Spanish Inquisition executions?
o: To clear the church completely
Because torture did not really exist
Because exaggeration damages the truth, and correcting numbers is not defending the crimes
quiz.e: Honesty works both ways: no exaggeration, and no downplaying.

quiz.q: How did Daniel face his people’s sin in his prayer?
o: He stood inside it and said, “We have sinned”
He accused others and declared himself innocent
He thought confession was unnecessary
quiz.e: He did not distance himself. This is also the posture for Christians facing church history.

units.title: The Great Revival at the End
units.sub: In 1900 Africa had about nine million Christians; in 2025, 750 million. God is doing something on a world scale, but no one knows the day.

share.v: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no man could count, out of every nation and of all tribes, peoples, and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands. They cried with a loud voice, saying, “Salvation be to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!”

blocks.h: In 1900, about 82 percent of the world’s Christians lived in the “Global North,” in Europe, North America and similar regions. By 2025, nearly 70 percent lived in Africa, Asia and Latin America.
Rarely in human history has a faith moved its center of gravity to another hemisphere in little more than a century. Today’s typical Christian may be a mother in Nigeria or a young person in Brazil.

After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no man could count, out of every nation and of all tribes, peoples, and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands. They cried with a loud voice, saying, “Salvation be to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!”
The map has moved

The Center for the Study of Global Christianity (Gordon-Conwell) estimates that African Christians grew from about 9.6 million in 1900 to about 750 million in 2025; Asia from about 22 million to about 420 million; Latin America from about 62 million to about 620 million; Europe stands at about 550 million, shrinking by about 0.5 percent a year. In 2002 Philip Jenkins had already pointed to this trend in The Next Christendom.
It is like a river changing course. People standing by the old channel see less and less water and think the river is drying up; people who walk to the new channel see a flood.

The other side of the numbers must be told too. A 2025 Pew Research Center report found that from 2010 to 2020 the number of Christians grew to about 2.3 billion, yet their share of the world’s population fell from 31 percent to 29 percent, one main reason being that many people leave the faith as adults. Christians in Australia have fallen to just under half; sub-Saharan Africa has overtaken Europe as the region with the most Christians.

Pew counts 2.3 billion (2020, self-identification from surveys and censuses), while the Center for the Study of Global Christianity counts 2.6 billion (2026, with a broader method). The definitions differ, so cite the source when quoting. Estimates of the number of Christians in China vary enormously, so be careful with any single figure.
Revivals in history

items: Northampton (1734–35): a wave of repentance in Jonathan Edwards’s parish, part of the Great Awakening. Edwards himself held slaves; in 1731 he bought a girl of about 14 named Venus.
Wales (1904–05): led by the miner Evan Roberts, with estimates of converts ranging from 80,000 to 160,000; many pubs fell quiet. Roberts later broke down from overwork and withdrew from public view.

Azusa Street (1906): in Los Angeles, led by Pastor William Seymour, the son of former slaves, where Black, white and Latino worshipers gathered; soon afterward Parham, out of racial prejudice, started his own meetings, and Seymour was nearly forgotten.

Pyongyang (1907): a January Bible conference of about 1,500 people, where Kil Sun-joo confessed his sin publicly and led the others into repentance, leaving behind the tradition of early-morning prayer. Today that city is the capital of North Korea.

Timor, Indonesia (from 1965): church membership grew greatly within two years, accompanied by political turmoil; several of the numbers and miracle testimonies that circulated at the time were questioned or corrected by investigators.

blocks.h: These revivals were all real, all imperfect, and none lasted forever.
Let’s look at each claim separately and mark how certain it is.
The center of gravity of the Christian population has clearly shifted south: in 2020 sub-Saharan Africa held about 31 percent of the world’s Christians, more than Europe’s 22 percent (Pew).

Christians in the Global South make up about 69 percent (2025), projected at about 78 percent in 2050. The estimates use clear methods, but the definition of a believer, the quality of the data and future trends all carry uncertainty.

The Christian share of the world’s population has dipped slightly in recent years; Pentecostals and charismatics are growing about 2 percent a year and evangelicals about 1.34 percent, higher than Christianity as a whole at 0.95 percent (2026 estimates). The numbers are affected by definitions.

The scale of individual revivals and their miracle testimonies are often exaggerated: estimates for Wales differ by a factor of two, and Timor’s numbers and several of its miracle testimonies were questioned. We should not repeat unverified numbers.

These trends are God’s work and point to a great revival at the end. This is a hope and interpretation of faith, which statistics can neither prove nor refute; sociologists can explain the same numbers by population and social change.
Perspectives Room
Does the Bible promise a great revival at the end? Evangelicals differ, and all hold that Christ will return in person.

items.h: Before Christ’s return the world will grow worse, and there may also be a large-scale gospel harvest; they often cite Matthew 24:12 and the rebellion of 2 Thessalonians 2:3. Some hold both sides together.
The church age is the age of Christ’s reign, and the gospel and evil run side by side until the Lord comes; they do not necessarily expect one final special revival, but always hope for God’s work.

The gospel will triumph greatly before the Lord’s return, bringing widespread renewal; they often cite the parable of the mustard seed and the Great Commission. Critics think this is too optimistic about history.
Christ will return; no one knows the day; the church should faithfully preach the gospel. The 321 vision hopes for a great revival at the end, and that hope needs no date to prop it up.

blocks.h: His Spirit poured out on all flesh
At Pentecost Peter quoted Joel and declared that “the last days” had begun. This period stretches from the birth of the church to the Lord’s return.
‘It will be in the last days, says God, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your young men will see visions. Your old men will dream dreams.
Jesus gave the church a task and refused to give it a timetable. The disciples asked, and His answer is still valid today.
This Good News of the Kingdom will be preached in the whole world for a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.
“But no one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, but my Father only.

The power of revival has never been ours. The source of all revival is the grain of wheat that fell into the ground. Christ died and rose again, and only then could His life bear fruit among every tribe and region. The song before the throne is ascribed to the Lamb.
Most certainly I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.

Open a world map and point to a place you have never been. Imagine that people there are singing to the same Lord today in a language you cannot understand. Be quiet for a minute and pray for them and for the place where you live.
Reflect: The revival I want, is it the church becoming lively, or God beginning His work in me?

Pray: Risen Lord, Your Spirit is at work in places far beyond what I can see. Revive me first, make me humble and repentant, and free me from being the center of my own world. We do not ask for dates; we ask only to be faithful. Raise up spiritual companions and comrades in arms, build God’s kingdom system, until all peoples hear the gospel. Lord Jesus, I long for You to come! In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Selflessness: Every revival begins with brokenness. The confession at Pyongyang and Daniel’s prayer remind me that for revival, my self must come down first.

235 relationships: Find a spiritual companion, a spiritual parent or child, and a comrade in arms, and pray and evangelize together. Revival does not depend on one hero, and Roberts’s exhaustion is the reminder.
Become an overcomer: Without watching dates or chasing excitement, let Jesus reign every day, and by the blood of the Lamb and the word of testimony, walk faithfully to the end.

blocks.h: This week: List three relatives or friends who do not yet know Jesus, pray for them every day this week, and invite one of them to a meal.
Pass it on: Did you know that most of the world’s Christians today live in Africa, Asia and Latin America? Why do you think that is?
Quiz

quiz.q: According to Matthew 24:36, who knows the day of the Lord’s return?
o: Those skilled in prophecy
The Father only
Church leaders, after they meet and decide
quiz.e: Jesus said plainly that no one knows, so any claim that announces a date must be rejected.

quiz.q: Which statement about global Christianity is most accurate?
o: The number and share of Christians are exploding everywhere
Global Christianity is disappearing entirely
The center of gravity has moved south, but the Christian share of the world’s population has dipped slightly in recent years
quiz.e: An honest picture shows both sides: rapid growth in Africa, and many people in the West leaving the faith.

quiz.q: From Edwards to Seymour, what reminder do the revivals of history give us?
o: Revivals are real, but participants still have sins and blind spots, and need continual repentance
The leaders of revival are flawless
Revival only brings growth in statistics
quiz.e: Edwards held slaves, and Azusa Street was troubled by racial division. Grace is real, and people still need to repent.

questions.q: What about all the harm Christians have done?
Is Christianity a Western religion? Did ancient China know Shangdi?

sub: From human dignity to the coming revival: twelve units on how the gospel changed the world, with an honest look at the church’s failures.
